scope: Independent disk-only diagnosis and in-memory lossless representation experiments. No product/source/harness edits, tests, models, web, installation, or commits.
conclusion: The observed failure does not require a larger model or new transport: a generic readable quoted-string reference representation fits this exact complete logical payload below the same input character limit. This is a diagnostic proof, not a production implementation or live success claim.

boundary.schema_note: Separate output-schema file. The provider actual_chars equals prompt alone exactly; no evidence that schema size caused this rejection.

attempt_note: Five attempts (0–4), four retries, same oversized prompt/schema; final discard/planning failure at trace 1879/1880, propagated refinement failure 1881. These failed attempts remain preserved.

root_causes.finding: Single-apostrophe prose can hide canonical JSON quoted spans from the current combined quote regex.
root_causes.evidence: In logical /trajectory/99/prompt (85,585 characters), the apostrophe in person's at offset 180 starts a 17,907-character single-quote match crossing into JSON source evidence. The old lexer finds only 1 double-quoted span; a double-only JSON lexer finds 84. No data is lost, but repeated evidence cannot be shared efficiently.

root_causes.finding: The same source exists as a raw fetched string and as JSON-escaped text embedded in different prompts; current exact-string sharing stores both forms.
root_causes.evidence: Canonical JSON-quote references to the raw string preserve every original character while avoiding this representational duplication.

root_causes.finding: Recursive factoring confined to the existing shared_texts literal table is insufficient on its own.
root_causes.evidence: Existing encoded payload contributes 1,330,910 compact JSON characters, while the table contributes 257,567. Even eliminating table storage entirely leaves at least 1,334,457 characters after existing planner/backend instructions, already above the provider limit. A broader DAG can help only if it also factors payload literals/substructures or equivalent escaped forms.

experiments.method: Canonical JSON-quote references with original combined quoted-span lexer
Apply current shared-text-v2 as an outer lossless factorization of the previous diagnostic representation
Canonical JSON / ASCII JSON / Python-repr references using original combined lexer
Double-only canonical JSON quoted-span segmentation plus references that render raw shared strings with exact json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) quoting
Apply current shared-text-v2 to the successful diagnostic representation, including its table strings

proposed_general_representation.description: Version the readable shared-text format. Preserve literal strings, exact concatenation, and escaped original objects; add an exact JSON-quote reference operation to a raw string (with explicit quote nesting if needed). Detect canonical JSON double-quoted spans independently of prose apostrophes. Every logical object key, scalar, list position, source text, prompt, code block, and evidence anchor remains recoverable.
proposed_general_representation.operation: Given raw shared string s and depth n, repeat json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False) n times, returning that exact resulting string; concatenate literal/reference pieces without separators. Accept a canonical quote span only when decoding and re-encoding reproduces the original span exactly.
proposed_general_representation.prototype_selection: The diagnostic used first-occurrence candidate ordering and a conservative 40-character reference-cost estimate to select potentially profitable raw strings, then measured the complete result. This is not a production cost model. Production selection should use exact serialized reference/table/wrapper costs and retain the smaller full representation, independent of provider limits.
required_implementation_validation: Exact full logical roundtrip, including reserved-marker collisions, nesting, Unicode, control characters, lone/escaped quotes, backslashes, empty strings, and noncanonical JSON spellings.
Strict malformed reference/type/depth validation; if a recursive table is used, backward references or explicit cycle rejection.
Measure actual final planner instructions + backend prefix + wire representation, and retain full schema/candidate accounting.
Replay every preserved failed/successful planner payload offline without dropping fields; use normal tests for source changes.
No source/site/task-specific rules, model or budget changes, root-prompt truncation, field projection, content normalization, binary compression, or cap-tuned selection.
limitations: Reported successful sizes retain old instructions as a common comparison; a production format needs revised instructions and their exact length must be included. There is approximately 199k characters of headroom for the simple successful prototype.

This proves only that the observed failed payload has enough lossless redundancy. Arbitrarily large unique inputs can still exceed finite transport limits; such a case would require an explicit transport design or a visible failure, not silent truncation.
No final new-cohort success or production readiness is asserted.
